assets.name: abrotonum-foemina
assets.description: The complete original abrotonum foemina botanical woodcut, retaining all connected stems, leaves, flowers and roots. Source captions and reverse-side printing excluded. Part of the Fuchs 1542 Herbal set.

provenance.title: Fuchs, De historia stirpium: Abrotonum foemina (scan [39])
provenance.image_rights: Public Domain Mark; parent bibliographic record

extraction.method: native ink coverage relative to locally measured paper; eight opacity contour layers
extraction.vector_method: Five-layer native ink-opacity contour tracing, 0.25px geometric approximation, genuine editable paths without raster embedding
extraction.tool: native source ink analysis / OpenCV editable contours
extraction.source_rgb_modified: Original printed ink isolated from measured scan paper, then represented by its measured ink tone and native opacity. No new leaves, stems, flowers, roots or ink shapes.

review.notes: Compared all printed branches, leaf/flower tips, fine stalks and roots against original scan and retained SVG render. Native ink geometry preserved, caption/reverse-page ghost text excluded, all unprinted paper transparent; extraction bytes unchanged.

assets.usage_notes: One plant with connected shoots and roots. Its branches are not separate plants and no repeat period is inferred. Transparent line artwork preserves the actual printed ink contours.

vector_review.method: Five-layer native ink-opacity contour tracing, 0.25px geometric approximation, genuine editable paths without raster embedding

previous_review.notes: Freshly inspected the complete source plant, native ink result and rendered SVG. Connected shoots and roots remain one illustration; captions and reverse-side page material are excluded. Weak original print lines are retained without inventing missing sections.

selection_history.reason: Normalize new staging metadata to shared category/composition/subject vocabulary; factual descriptions and original source metadata unchanged.

sets.relation: same historical botanical volume and illustration style
